title: Clarinetists in town in the 1920s: Humphrey, Lewis, Handy, Burbank
summary: Barnes recalls whether Willie Humphrey, George Lewis, John Handy and Albert Burbank were around and respected in the 1920s.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: If you think back in the twenties, some of the fellas who were still in town. Could you remember if they had big reputations or not, like somebody like Willie Humphreys, was he considered good in your 20s? I didn't hear much of Willie Humphreys. Of course he was out of town a lot in the 20s too. How about George Lewis?
George wasn't in, I don't think. He wasn't around too much. No, I just remember George. What about Andy?
I had him with him before.
Did he play radio or was he a reader?

He's a fast, good dog. I don't think he was no reader. No, he's not no reader, because there's very few people that read down here who don't be reading now too much. But I know he's a good clownish player. How about Israel Gorman? Israel wasn't nowhere. No, he wasn't nowhere. Steve, I don't know if I was. Steve?
Steve Anger? Yeah. But Handy was considered better than those guys?
Handy, oh Handy, yeah. Handy was good. His friends, yes. Now there's a couple more.

How about Albert Burbank? Did you hear anything about him in the 20s? Albert wasn't out. No. No. Albert wasn't young. Talk about it at all. He didn't play with bands that were... Well, I don't know no bands that were...
Well, I don't know no bands that were... Outside of the young bands when it started. Yeah, that's all I know.
